584.d: Swallowing large amounts of water, they make snow clouds inside their bodies and attack their foes with violent blizzards.

585.d: The color and scent of their fur changes to match the mountain grass. When they sense hostility, they hide in the grass.

586.d: They migrate according to the seasons. People can tell the season by looking at Sawsbuck’s horns.

587.d: The energy made in its cheeks’ electric pouches is stored inside its membrane and released while it is gliding.

588.d: These mysterious Pokémon evolve when they receive electrical stimulation while they are in the same place as Shelmet.

589.d: They fly around at high speed, striking with their pointed spears. Even when in trouble, they face opponents bravely.

590.d: It lures people in with its Poké Ball pattern, then releases poison spores. Why it resembles a Poké Ball is unknown.

591.d: It lures prey close by dancing and waving its arm caps, which resemble Poké Balls, in a swaying motion.

592.d: With its thin, veil-like arms wrapped around the body of its opponent, it sinks to the ocean floor.

593.d: The fate of the ships and crew that wander into Jellicent’s habitat: all sunken, all lost, all vanished.

594.d: The special membrane enveloping Alomomola has the ability to heal wounds.

595.d: Joltik that live in cities have learned a technique for sucking electricity from the outlets in houses.

596.d: When attacked, they create an electric barrier by spitting out many electrically charged threads.

597.d: When threatened, it attacks by shooting a barrage of spikes, which gives it a chance to escape by rolling away.

598.d: It fights by swinging around its three spiky feelers. A hit from these steel spikes can reduce a boulder to rubble.

599.d: The two minigears that mesh together are predetermined. Each will rebound from other minigears without meshing.

600.d: By changing the direction in which it rotates, it communicates its feelings to others. When angry, it rotates faster.

601.d: Its red core functions as an energy tank. It fires the charged energy through its spikes into an area.

602.d: While one alone doesn’t have much power, a chain of many Tynamo can be as powerful as lightning.

603.d: They coil around foes and shock them with electricity-generating organs that seem simply to be circular patterns.

604.d: They crawl out of the ocean using their arms. They will attack prey on shore and immediately drag it into the ocean.

605.d: It uses its strong psychic power to squeeze its opponent’s brain, causing unendurable headaches.

606.d: It can manipulate an opponent’s memory. Apparently, it communicates by flashing its three different-colored fingers.

607.d: Litwick shines a light that absorbs the life energy of people and Pokémon, which becomes the fuel that it burns.

608.d: This ominous Pokémon is feared. Through cities it wanders, searching for the spirits of the fallen.

609.d: It absorbs a spirit, which it then burns. By waving the flames on its arms, it puts its foes into a hypnotic trance.

610.d: They use their tusks to crush the berries they eat. Repeated regrowth makes their tusks strong and sharp.

611.d: Since a broken tusk will not grow back, they diligently sharpen their tusks on river rocks after they’ve been fighting.

612.d: They are kind but can be relentless when defending territory. They challenge foes with tusks that can cut steel.

613.d: When it is not feeling well, its mucus gets watery and the power of its Ice-type moves decreases.

614.d: It can make its breath freeze at will. Very able in the water, it swims around in northern seas and catches prey.

615.d: When its body temperature goes up, it turns into steam and vanishes. When its temperature lowers, it returns to ice.

616.d: When attacked, it defends itself by closing the lid of its shell. It can spit a sticky, poisonous liquid.

617.d: When its body dries out, it weakens. So, to prevent dehydration, it wraps itself in many layers of thin membrane.

618.d: Its skin is very hard, so it is unhurt even if stepped on by sumo wrestlers. It smiles when transmitting electricity.

619.d: In fights, they dominate with onslaughts of flowing, continuous attacks. With their sharp claws, they cut enemies.

620.d: It wields the fur on its arms like a whip. Its arm attacks come with such rapidity that they cannot even be seen.

621.d: It warms its body by absorbing sunlight with its wings. When its body temperature falls, it can no longer move.

622.d: The energy that burns inside it enables it to move, but no one has yet been able to identify this energy.

623.d: It flies across the sky at Mach speeds. Removing the seal on its chest makes its internal energy go out of control.

624.d: Blades comprise this Pokémon’s entire body. If battling dulls the blades, it sharpens them on stones by the river.

625.d: It leads a group of Pawniard. It battles to become the boss, but will be driven from the group if it loses.

626.d: Their fluffy fur absorbs damage, even if they strike foes with a fierce headbutt.

627.d: They crush berries with their talons. They bravely stand up to any opponent, no matter how strong it is.

628.d: They fight for their friends without any thought about danger to themselves. One can carry a car while flying.

629.d: Its wings are too tiny to allow it to fly. As the time approaches for it to evolve, it discards the bones it was wearing.

630.d: It makes a nest out of bones it finds. It grabs weakened prey in its talons and hauls it to its nest of bones.

631.d: It breathes through a hole in its tail while it burns with an internal fire. Durant is its prey.

632.d: They attack in groups, covering themselves in steel armor to protect themselves from Heatmor.

633.d: It tends to bite everything, and it is not a picky eater. Approaching it carelessly is dangerous.

634.d: After it has eaten up all the food in its territory, it moves to another area. Its two heads do not get along.

635.d: This brutal Pokémon travels the skies on its six wings. Anything that moves seems like a foe to it, triggering its attack.

636.d: This Pokémon was believed to have been born from the sun. When it evolves, its entire body is engulfed in flames.

637.d: When volcanic ash darkened the atmosphere, it is said that Volcarona’s fire provided a replacement for the sun.

638.d: This legendary Pokémon battled against humans to protect Pokémon. Its personality is calm and composed.

639.d: This Pokémon came to the defense of Pokémon that had lost their homes in a war among humans.

640.d: This Pokémon fought humans in order to protect its friends. Legends about it continue to be passed down.

641.d: The lower half of its body is wrapped in a cloud of energy. It zooms through the sky at 200 mph.

642.d: Countless charred remains mar the landscape of places through which Thundurus has passed.

643.d: This Pokémon appears in legends. It sends flames into the air from its tail, burning up everything around it.

644.d: Concealing itself in lightning clouds, it flies throughout the Unova region. It creates electricity in its tail.

645.d: Lands visited by Landorus grant such bountiful crops that it has been hailed as “The Guardian of the Fields.”

646.d: It generates a powerful, freezing energy inside itself, but its body became frozen when the energy leaked out.

647.d: By blasting water from its hooves, it can glide across water. It excels at using leg moves while battling.

648.d: Its melodies are sung with a special vocalization method that can control the feelings of those who hear it.

649.d: Over 300 million years ago, it was feared as the strongest of hunters. It has been modified by Team Plasma.
